posts.text: Thank you! In logistics, ‘Asset light’ seems more like a single edged sword than double edged in many other businesses - cuts the asset light operator more often than the asset heavy. VRL realised it very early and went asset heavy. Managing the asset is a science in logistics and most who wanted it to be outsourced to less skilled ‘contract’ vehicle owners suffered heavily. I haven’t studied SJ, but what I gathered from your inputs is: Transaction management in a specific part of logistics is what gives SJ its edge. Positioning: Asset-Light Operational Specialist, Not an Identity Crisis SJ isn’t trying to be Adani (port infrastructure), GE Shipping (asset-heavy balance sheet), or Porter/Delhivery (last-mile aggregator). Like many expanding logistics businesses, it is moving up the value chain from transactional port agency to an integrated maritime operations partner. The goal is to capture higher revenue per port call and vessel turnaround without deploying billions in hard vessel ownership. 2. posts.text: Competitive landscape: Can you please clarify if ‘pure play’ masking the real competition. All multimodal logistics providers seem to be doing what they are doing.
